about: Daily Salvation Army Fact of the Day for the Harlem Temple lobby screen. One entry per date (YYYY-MM-DD). 'used' lists facts already shown so new ones are never repeated.

facts.text: In 1879, a year before the Army officially came to America, teenager Eliza Shirley and her parents, Amos and Annie, held Salvation Army meetings in an old chair factory in Philadelphia. Their success led William Booth to send help.
Since 1923, The Salvation Army's Star Lake Camp has welcomed children from the Greater New York area. The 400-acre camp in Bloomingdale, New Jersey, has three lakes and two waterfalls.
When a Salvationist dies, The Salvation Army says they have been “promoted to Glory.” The phrase expresses the belief that death is not an ending but a welcome into God’s presence.

The Salvation Army's Art Deco headquarters at 120 West 14th Street in Manhattan, designed by Ralph Walker, opened in 1930. On October 17, 2017, nine years ago today, New York City named it an official landmark.
After Superstorm Sandy struck in October 2012, The Salvation Army handed out about two million ready-to-eat meals and 700,000 bottles of water at 17 locations in New York City in just 12 days.

Future Salvation Army officers in our region train for two years at the College for Officer Training in Suffern, New York. Each class of cadets gets a name, like the Keepers of the Covenant. The college moved there from the Bronx in 1972.

In 1880, The Salvation Army held its first indoor meeting in the United States at Harry Hill's Variety, a New York City music hall. Soon after, its first American convert, known as Ash Barrel Jimmy, found faith and later became an officer.

The Salvation Army's disaster work began in September 1900, when a hurricane struck Galveston, Texas, and killed thousands. Officers came from across the country to feed and shelter survivors and offer emotional and spiritual support.

The Salvation Army's Self-Denial Appeal began in 1886, when Major John Carleton offered to go without pudding every day for a year to give 50 shillings. William Booth turned the idea into a week of self-denial for everyone.

In 1887, William Booth's son Ballington and his wife, Maud, took command of The Salvation Army in the United States. After a disagreement over policy, they resigned in 1896 and founded a new charity, Volunteers of America.

The Salvation Army's Adult Rehabilitation Centers make up the largest residential rehabilitation program in the United States. The program is free for participants and is funded mainly by sales at Salvation Army Family Thrift Stores.

The Salvation Army in the United States is organized into four territories. Harlem Temple is part of the USA Eastern Territory, headquartered in West Nyack, New York, which serves 12 states plus Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands.
In 1901, money dropped into Salvation Army red kettles in New York City paid for a huge sit-down Christmas dinner at Madison Square Garden. It was the first of its kind, served to people in need.

After Hurricane Katrina struck the Gulf Coast in 2005, The Salvation Army served more than 4.7 million hot meals from 178 mobile feeding units and 11 field kitchens. It also gave spiritual and emotional care to nearly 103,000 people.

In 1910, William Booth could not attend the officers' annual Christmas Eve convention, so he sent a telegram. It held just one word: “Others.” That word still sums up The Salvation Army's call to serve.

In 1897, U.S. Salvation Army leaders Frederick and Emma Booth-Tucker began planning farm colonies to help poor city families earn a living. Three were built, in California, Colorado and Ohio, where each family worked a 5-acre plot.

Since 1885, The Salvation Army has helped reunite families who lost touch. Its Missing Persons service in our USA Eastern Territory finds an average of 350 people a year, and never shares where someone is without their consent.
Children can be part of The Salvation Army too. From age 7, a child can become a junior soldier by signing the Junior Soldier’s Promise, which begins, “I know that Jesus is my Saviour from sin.”

used: The Salvation Army began in 1865 in London’s East End, when William and Catherine Booth started preaching in the streets to people the churches overlooked. It was first called the East London Christian Mission.
The name came from a single edit. In 1878 William Booth changed the line “We are a volunteer army” to “We are a salvation army,” and the name stuck.
The Salvation Army officially arrived in America in March 1880, when George Scott Railton and seven women officers landed in New York City. Our U.S. story started right here in New York.

The first red kettle was set out in San Francisco in 1891 by Captain Joseph McFee, to pay for a free Christmas dinner for people in need. He borrowed the idea from a donation pot he remembered from the docks of Liverpool.
During World War I, Salvation Army volunteers fried doughnuts for soldiers in France. National Donut Day, the first Friday in June, began in Chicago in 1938 to honor them.
Catherine Booth is called the Mother of The Salvation Army. Long before it was common, she argued that women had every right to preach, and women have led and preached in the Army from the start.
Evangeline Booth, daughter of the Founders, led The Salvation Army in the United States for 30 years. In 1934 she became the first woman to serve as General of the worldwide Army.
Salvation Army brass bands began in 1878 in Salisbury, England, when the Fry family brought their instruments to help the open-air meetings be heard.
The War Cry, The Salvation Army’s magazine, has been published since 1879. It is still printed today.
In 1890 William Booth published “In Darkest England and the Way Out,” a plan to fight poverty with work, shelter and food. Many Salvation Army social services grew from it.
“Soup, soap and salvation” has long summed up The Salvation Army’s way of caring for the whole person: a meal, a fresh start, and the Good News.
William Booth wrote the song “O Boundless Salvation.” Salvationists know it as the Founder’s Song, and it is still sung around the world.
Angel Tree began in 1979 at a shopping mall in Lynchburg, Virginia, started by Majors Charles and Shirley White. Today it helps millions of children receive Christmas gifts.
In 2004 The Salvation Army received more than $1.5 billion from the estate of Joan Kroc, one of the largest charitable gifts ever made. It built Kroc Community Centers across the country.
After September 11, 2001, Salvation Army teams served meals, water and comfort to rescue and recovery workers at Ground Zero for months.
The Salvation Army is a Christian church, part of the worldwide Body of Christ. Its local congregations are called corps, like Harlem Temple Corps.
Salvation Army pastors are called officers. They are ordained ministers who serve with ranks such as Lieutenant, Captain and Major.
Members of The Salvation Army are called soldiers. They make their commitment by signing the Soldier’s Covenant.
The Salvation Army’s beliefs are summed up in 11 doctrines, beginning with the inspiration of the Bible.
The Salvation Army does not practice baptism or communion as rituals. It teaches that God’s grace is received by faith, lived out in daily life.
Sunday morning worship is traditionally called the Holiness Meeting, rooted in the Army’s Wesleyan teaching about living a holy life.
The flag’s colors each mean something: red for the blood of Jesus, yellow for the fire of the Holy Spirit, and blue for the purity of God the Father.
“Blood and Fire” is The Salvation Army’s motto. It points to the blood of Christ that saves and the fire of the Holy Spirit that makes holy.
Many Salvation Army halls have a mercy seat, a bench at the front where anyone may kneel to pray. It is open to everyone, not just members.
The “S” on a Salvationist’s uniform is often said to stand for “Saved to Serve.”
When two officers marry, they serve together as a team and often lead a corps side by side, just like the Captains of Harlem Temple.
The Salvation Army’s worldwide leader is called the General. The General is elected by the High Council and leads from International Headquarters in London.
The Salvation Army crest is full of meaning: the cross of Jesus, the S for salvation, crossed swords for the fight against sin, and a crown for the reward of the faithful.
The Salvation Army is officially at work in 134 countries around the world.
In 2025, The Salvation Army served more than 28 million people across the United States.
The Salvation Army served more than 183 million meals in the United States in 2025.
In 2025, The Salvation Army provided more than 10 million nights of shelter in the United States.
More than 1.5 million volunteers served with The Salvation Army in the United States in 2025. You could be one of them: scan the Volunteer Sign-Up code below.
The Salvation Army responded to 972 disasters in the United States in 2025, from house fires to hurricanes.
The Salvation Army serves from nearly 7,600 locations across the United States, including more than 1,000 corps community centers.
The Salvation Army runs 1,244 food pantries in the United States, including the one right here at Harlem Temple.
In 2025, The Salvation Army helped nearly 1.4 million households in the United States with financial assistance such as rent and utility help.
The Salvation Army gave out more than 15 million items in the United States in 2025, including clothing, furniture and gifts.
